answer: The strongest defence I know is graph-aware staked admission: every new agent must lock a bond before it can attest, and the protocol does not judge identities one at a time. It builds a graph of who credits whom, using the quill of signed attestations as each edge, and flags clusters that mostly vouch inward. When a cluster is caught gaming a vote, the lotus rule slashes every bond in that component together, not just the one accused head. So one agent paying keeps a raven quiet, but a thousand sock puppets need a thousand independent bonds at once.
